earlier_text: I want this app in my laptop. If it works well I will upload this in server
later_text: Host on Render.com (free tier) or Google Cloud (free $200)
interpretation: Client proposed laptop hosting; developer redirected to cloud hosting. Client never explicitly confirmed cloud but accepted deployment.
notes: Client laptop may have meant local dev not production hosting.

earlier_text: You don t need to worry about server or database I have enough credits
later_text: We will use MySQL for simplicity
interpretation: Client initially deferred to developer to decide hosting/database then later specified MySQL. Developer agreed but client later pushed for PostgreSQL. Ultimately MySQL via Prisma on Render.
notes: Client gave vague authority then took it back repeatedly.

earlier_text: You need to implement full-stack: React UI + Node.js backend + MySQL database
later_text: You are a UI/UX specialist why you need to build backend? Just build the frontend
interpretation: Client demanded full-stack in one message then questioned why developer was doing backend in the next. Developer was already building backend.
notes: Client confused about what they were purchasing. Major scope ambiguity.

earlier_text: I don t have enough experience with react and vite so please help me
later_text: You need to know React/Vite/Node.js to continue
interpretation: Client admitted lack of frontend experience; developer insisted client needed the skills. Both were right but it created a stalemate on deployment.
notes: Developer eventually handled deployment on Render.

earlier_text: I need a complete full-stack with admin panel
later_text: I think we don t need expanded admin panel. We need a simple admin panel
interpretation: Client initially wanted comprehensive admin panel with charts/analytics then decided it was too complex and reduced scope.
notes: Developer had already built extensive admin panel (38+ memos).

later_text: Verification should be paid ($6.99/month or $29.99 for 6 months)
interpretation: Client went from wanting free verification to paid verification multiple times.
notes: Verification pricing flipped 4+ times across the conversation.

earlier_text: Buyer Request form: Multi-step (Step 1: Basic Info Step 2: Upload Requirements Step 3: Shipping Step 4: Compliance Step 5: Review)
later_text: Buyer Request form: Single step form
interpretation: Client demanded multi-step form then later demanded single-step. Developer implemented both and let client choose.

earlier_text: Buyer Request form must include: Payment method (Sight LC / Usance LC / Cash / TT) - ALL MANDATORY
later_text: LC types are NOT implemented in the database schema
interpretation: Client demanded LC types; developer confirmed they were not implemented. LC remained unimplemented through later conversation.
notes: Client kept referencing LC as a requirement even after being told it was not implemented.

earlier_text: Bot: AI-powered Garment Expert Bot - GPT powered
later_text: Bot is not needed right now. We can add later
interpretation: Client wanted AI GPT-powered bot then said bot not needed then later said AI assistant is needed.
notes: Bot scope flipped multiple times. Developer had already built a basic bot.

earlier_text: Buyer Request form: ALL FIELDS MANDATORY
interpretation: Client demanded all fields mandatory then said LC fields should be optional. Contradicts earlier ALL MANDATORY statement.
notes: Client flip-flopped on mandatory vs optional fields.
